title.narrative: Group on Earth Observation (GEO) - Global Ecosystems Atlas Phase 1

description.narrative:
The Global Ecosystems Atlas initiative will create a comprehensive, trusted map of the world's ecosystems using high-resolution Earth observation data and AI/ML technologies. It will integrate and standardize existing data, fill knowledge gaps, and provide tools to support global, regional, and national ecosystem assessments, reporting, and natural capital accounting. The Atlas will be accessible via an online platform, offering dynamic functionalities and data for public and private sector users to facilitate nature-positive planning and decision-making.
During the pilot phase (2025-2026), the project will develop a curated data catalogue of ecosystem-related spatial datasets and an open-access training dataset of confirmed ecosystem occurrence records. It will then create a Global Ecosystems Atlas basemap, filling data gaps through remote sensing and ecological modelling. The online platform will be developed to provide user-friendly access to this information, with comprehensive user support and a communication campaign to promote its use.
The Atlas will provide crucial data for planning and implementing nature-based solutions to climate adaptation. For example, it will identify areas suitable for reforestation to sequester carbon and improve ecosystem health, pinpoint riverbanks for restoring native vegetation to reduce flood risks, and map coastal ecosystems like mangroves and coral reefs that protect against natural disasters. By enhancing the capacity of low-income countries to manage and conserve their ecosystems, the Atlas will help mitigate the impacts of climate change, support sustainable livelihoods, and improve the quality of life for local communities. As an open digital public good, the Atlas will foster informed decision-making.
